## Overview

In the Ross–Macdonald model of malaria, infection passes from humans to mosquitoes and
back. There are two states-at-infection (`I_H` and `I_V`) and no within-type transmission,
so `K` is `2 × 2` with a zero diagonal and `R₀ = √(K[1,2] K[2,1])`. The square root
reflects a choice: counting a mosquito infected by a human as a "new infection" makes a
human-to-human cycle two generations long. Diekmann et al. (2010, section 3.1 and appendix A) emphasise that
different decompositions into transmissions and transitions give different reproduction
numbers, all with the same threshold. This vignette shows both.

## The model

```{julia}
using ReproductiveNumbers, ModelingToolkit, Symbolics
using ModelingToolkit: t_nounits as t, D_nounits as D

@parameters a b c γ μᵥ N_H N_V
@variables S_H(t) I_H(t) S_V(t) I_V(t)
eqs = [D(S_H) ~ -a * b * S_H * I_V / N_H + γ * I_H,
    D(I_H) ~ a * b * S_H * I_V / N_H - γ * I_H,
    D(S_V) ~ μᵥ * N_V - a * c * S_V * I_H / N_H - μᵥ * S_V,
    D(I_V) ~ a * c * S_V * I_H / N_H - μᵥ * I_V]
malaria = complete(System(eqs, t; name = :ross_macdonald))
```

Here `a` is the biting rate per mosquito, `b` and `c` the transmission probabilities per
bite (mosquito to human and human to mosquito), `γ` the human recovery rate and `μᵥ` the
mosquito death rate. The host population has no demography, so we supply the
infection-free state explicitly.

```{julia}
eq = Dict(S_H => N_H, S_V => N_V)
ngm = next_generation_matrix(malaria, [I_H, I_V]; equilibrium = eq)
```

## Two states-at-infection

```{julia}
ngm.K
```

`K[1, 2] = a b / μᵥ` is the number of humans infected by one mosquito over its lifetime and
`K[2, 1] = a c (N_V / N_H) / γ` the number of mosquitoes infected by one human. The
dominant eigenvalue of a `2 × 2` matrix with zero diagonal is the geometric mean:

```{julia}
R0 = basic_reproduction_number(ngm)
```

The `2 × 2` closed form `(tr K + √((K₁₁ - K₂₂)² + 4 K₁₂ K₂₁)) / 2`, and its reduction
to `√(K₁₂ K₂₁)` when the diagonal vanishes, are proved in
`proofs/ReproductiveNumbersProofs/TwoByTwo.lean`.

## Counting only host-to-host generations

If we regard only *human* infections as reproduction, then a human infecting a mosquito
is a transition, not a transmission. We tell the package which terms are new infections by
giving the vector of new-infection rates for each infected compartment (van den Driessche
and Watmough's `𝓕`):

```{julia}
ngm_host = next_generation_matrix(malaria, [I_H, I_V]; equilibrium = eq,
    transmission = [a * b * S_H * I_V / N_H, 0])
states_at_infection(ngm_host)
```

Now only `I_H` is a state-at-infection, `K` is `1 × 1`, and the reproduction number is
the square of the previous one, the classical Macdonald formula:

```{julia}
basic_reproduction_number(ngm_host)
```

```{julia}
symbolic_isequal(basic_reproduction_number(ngm_host), R0^2)
```

Both decompositions are legitimate; they agree on whether `R₀` exceeds one, but not on its
value. The transition matrix of the second decomposition is no longer block diagonal:
`-Σ⁻¹` now tracks a human's expected "time" spent as an infected mosquito.

```{julia}
ngm_host.Σ
```

## Numeric comparison

```{julia}
vals = Dict(a => 0.3, b => 0.5, c => 0.5, γ => 0.1, μᵥ => 0.1, N_H => 1000.0, N_V => 5000.0)
(basic_reproduction_number(ngm, vals), basic_reproduction_number(ngm_host, vals))
```

```{julia}
using LinearAlgebra
num = evaluate(ngm, vals)
# the Jacobian of the infected subsystem is the same for both decompositions
maximum(real, eigvals(num.T + num.Σ)) > 0
```
